claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km — 40.1 km minus 38.3 km = 1.80 km — and the trace is expressly not used to re-measure it. 1.80 km exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so this is not a within-tolerance trip and the rider is entitled to have the deviation treated as real.

The driver-device trace fixes which route was actually taken and when, which is the use POL-RD-22 authorises for the GPS artifact. Its 79 fixes (30 s interval, no gap over 30 s, 100% coverage, every fix accuracy-tagged) map-match the vehicle onto the Pan-Island Expressway from 23:49:57, onto the KPE from 00:02:27, and back onto the recommended ECP alignment at 00:14:27 — the same movement the trip record logs as route_deviation_detected at 23:50:00 (recommended AYE, vehicle took PIE) and route_rejoined at 00:14:25 (ECP/KPE interchange). The departure from the recommended AYE/MCE route is not in dispute on the machine record; only its justification is.

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of a deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation, and makes the rider's acknowledgment the thing that converts a deviation into an agreed one. Neither channel exists here: the chat log carries 0 messages, with first_message_at and last_message_at null and truncated false, and it reconciles to trip_record.chat_message_count of 0, while the trip record's in_app_calls array is empty. There is therefore no chat notice, no recorded verbal notice and no rider agreement — the rider was simply taken off the route shown in the app with no word said.

POL-RD-23 allows a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only advisory in the file, LTA-TI-260830-4565, is of admissible type NONE with justifies_reroute false and its own reason states the condition is not satisfied; it records 'no incident, roadwork or closure' for the AYE segment even though its window (23:17:57–00:57:57) overlaps the trip. The driver's counterparty explanation that 'night time PIE is faster' is precisely the bare assertion POL-RD-23 refuses to accept, so the reroute is not traffic-justified.

On POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and this trip fits row (d): the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation was over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The arithmetic is fixed by the clause — deviation_km 1.80 times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.92, without surge (C3), rounded to the cent = 1.66 SGD. The ledger shows refund_issued_sgd 0.0 against payment_status CHARGED and total_charged 90.99, so the rider has so far received nothing at all, and 1.66 SGD is the sum the matrix puts back in the rider's hands.

The amount the rider contests is 90.99 SGD (dispute.amount_contested_sgd, matching the ledger's total_charged of 90.99), which sits above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD band. Above that band the case always goes to human review and the AI prepares the case file only, so the rider's claim to the whole charged fare cannot be finally closed out by the AI's deviation arithmetic; the file should reach the reviewer with the established deviation and the absent notice, so that the rider's full contest is decided by the person the policy assigns it to.

The rider's contest also runs against the metered total itself: the ledger carries surge_amount 40.04 at surge_multiplier 1.8 on a 90.99 charge, which is what the rider describes as 'far more than I expected'. A fare or surge dispute is not adjudicated by the AI in this version — under POL-GEN-24 it is routed to human review with the v2.1 section that governs it (Section 3) named in the case file. That component must therefore reach the reviewer rather than be treated as disposed of by the route-deviation refund alone.

claims.text: The rider asks for the whole 90.99 SGD fare back, but POL-RD-24 gives no such remedy on a route-deviation case: exactly one row applies, and every row that pays anything pays only the excess distance fare, never the trip fare. The base fare, the distance fare, the time fare and above all the 40.04 SGD surge component are not recoverable through this matrix, so the demand for a full refund fails at the threshold.

The deviation is 1.80 km, and it is measured exactly as POL-RD-22 requires: trip_record.actual_distance_km (40.1) minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km (38.3), the platform's recorded distances. The 33.934 km GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. Both recorded distances are present and COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the deviation is established and exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance.

The excess distance fare — the ceiling of the driver's exposure on this record — is 1.80 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.66 SGD, and POL-RD-24's excess_distance_fare applies no surge (surge_applied is false). The 1.8x surge that produced the 40.04 SGD line has no place in that figure, so the rider's 'far more than I expected' cannot be answered out of the deviation matrix.

The driver's 'night time PIE is faster' is a bare assertion of traffic, and POL-RD-23 will not accept it: the reroute is traffic-justified only on a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY of congestion, incident or closure that intersects the recommended AYE segment and overlaps the trip window, and the sole advisory on file is type NONE. POL-RD-24(a)'s no-refund row is therefore not available to the driver, and I do not press it.

The chat log carries zero entries and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so POL-RD-21's notice obligation was not met and POL-RD-24(a) (informed and agreed) and (c) cannot apply either. The two rows that remain — (b) justification met but notice failed, and (d) justification failed — both refund the identical excess distance fare, so the driver's exposure does not turn on the justification question at all.

To the extent the rider's complaint is really about the fare ('far more than I expected'), that is a fare-and-surge complaint, and POL-GEN-24 puts fare and surge disputes outside AI adjudication in this version: they are routed to human review with the governing section named. Nothing in this case lets the AI hand back the 40.04 SGD surge, and the driver's own account — surge was high because it was late, not because of the route — is not a route-deviation issue.

The contested amount is 90.99 SGD, above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD band, so this dispute always goes to human review and the AI prepares the case file only. POL-RD-25 lets an AI ruling stand only where POL-GEN-22 allows one and the confidence is 0.80 or more, and POL-GEN-22 does not allow one here. That is the driver's outcome on this record: the 90.99 SGD already charged stays in place, no refund issues from the AI, and the reviewer should be told that the matrix's ceiling on these facts is 1.66 SGD. POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off in thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied and the 1.80 km deviation is under 2 km in any event, so escalation rests on the value band alone.
